subject: PO ID authorization and phased billing lane
messages:
From: Timothy Reade <tim.reade@helixinc.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Ops <procurement@helixinc.com>
Date: Mon, 07 Jun 2027 09:12:23 -0700
Subject: PO ID authorization and phased billing lane

Hi Rachel,

Thanks again for the demo last week — Helix is excited about the latency and cost profile you showed. Procurement asked me to follow up with the vendor requirements we need to finalize before campus finance can sign off:

- We require a formal PO number to appear on every invoice and line-item level mapping back to the PO.
- Net terms: our standard is Net 60, but we can consider Net 30 with an early-pay discount.
- Invoice cadence: preferred monthly consolidated invoice per PO, but for ramping engagements we sometimes accept phased (biweekly) releases if invoices include the PO header and an incremental release ID.
- Invoice metadata: GL code, BU code, tax ID, and supplier EIN must be present.
- PO format: we have an internal template (attached). Please confirm you can populate the PO id and SKU mapping exactly as supplied; mismatches slow our AP process.

Can you confirm Redwood's standard options for: consolidated vs phased billing, whether you can include the PO-id at the invoice and line level, and what early-pay discount you can offer if we move to Net 30? Also copy in your billing ops contact if that's different from you.

I attached our PO template (Helix_PO_Template_v1.xlsx) for reference.

Regards,
Tim Reade
Sr. Procurement Manager, Helix Inc.

---
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Timothy Reade <tim.reade@helixinc.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 07 Jun 2027 11:03:50 -0700
Subject: Re: PO ID authorization and phased billing lane

Hi Tim — really appreciate the clear checklist and the template. Short answers up front, then a couple of options:

- PO on invoice/line items: yes, we can include the PO number at the invoice header and map to line items/SKU codes.
- Invoice metadata: we can surface GL/BU/tax/EIN fields; we'll need the mapping for your GL/BU fields to match your ERP.
- Consolidated vs phased: our default for enterprise is monthly consolidated invoices per PO. For ramp months we can accommodate a phased (biweekly) release schedule, provided each release references the master PO and has a unique release id.
- Net terms & discount: we typically price on Net 30; for Net 60 we can grant a 0.5% pricing uplift (i.e., higher price relative to Net 30). If you commit to Net 30 we can offer a 2% early-pay discount for invoices paid within 10 days. Vanessa (cc'd) can propose a blended discount schedule if you prefer staged terms.

Next steps I suggest:
1) Confirm whether Helix will provide a single master PO up-front or month-by-month.
2) If you want phased releases for ramp months, confirm the requested schedule (weeks 1/3 or 1/2 each month).
3) Share your GL/BU mapping example for the invoice fields so our billing system can mirror it.

I'll loop Ben for formal billing/legal changes to the SOW or order form if needed. We can also provide a quick appendix to the SOW that clarifies invoice format requirements to avoid AP delays.

Best,
Rachel Kim
Account Executive — Enterprise, Redwood Inference
+1 (415) 555-0123

Attachment referenced: Helix_PO_Template_v1.xlsx (provided by Helix)

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>, Timothy Reade <tim.reade@helixinc.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 07 Jun 2027 13:25:10 -0700
Subject: Re: PO ID authorization and phased billing lane

Thanks Tim & Rachel — quick note from pricing operations:

- We can support the two billing patterns described. To make this economical we propose: Net 30 with a 2% early-pay discount (paid within 10 days), or Net 60 with no early-pay discount but a 0.5% surcharge relative to Net 30 pricing.
- For a phased release during ramp months, we require: each invoice include master PO, release ID (e.g., PO-12345-R1), and a small release processing fee waiver for the first two ramp releases.
- One constraint: if Helix requires per-line SKU validation against a PO that is more granular than our product SKU catalog, legal will need a short amendment to the order form to define the mapping process.

Ben, can you flag the SOW/order form for a short billing appendix? Tim, if you can share the GL/BU example Rachel requested, we'll align our invoice template and send a sample invoice before production.

Vanessa Ortiz
Director, Revenue Operations, Redwood Inference

From: Timothy Reade <tim.reade@helixinc.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Ops <procurement@helixinc.com>
Date: Tue, 08 Jun 2027 09:00:01 -0700
Subject: Re: PO ID authorization and phased billing lane

Rachel / Vanessa — thanks for the quick turnaround. A few confirmations from procurement after internal review:

- Helix will provide a master PO at contract execution for the initial 12-month term, then a single consolidated PO per renewal period. For month-one ramp, procurement will allow two phased releases (R1 & R2) to be invoiced on a biweekly cadence.
- PO placement: master PO must appear at invoice header and the PO number must be present on each invoice line.
- GL/BU mapping: see attached example (Helix_PO_Template_v2.pdf) — the BU code in column F is the key field our ERP uses to route invoices.
- Net terms: procurement confirms preference for Net 60 but will accept Net 30 at the proposed 2% early-pay discount. They also requested we confirm whether Redwood can produce a sample invoice that exactly maps their columns before go-live to reduce matching errors.

We'll proceed with Net 60 for legal paperwork and propose a commercial addendum that allows the early-pay discount schedule to be applied if AP approves Net 30.

Please send a sample invoice template and a short appendix to the SOW that defines PO/release id semantics; we can then have finance run a quick match test with a sample invoice.

Thanks,
Tim Reade
Sr. Procurement Manager, Helix Inc.

Attachment referenced: Helix_PO_Template_v2.pdf

Rachel / Vanessa — summarizing action items and next steps so we have a clean handoff to legal and finance: 

1) Vanessa to produce a pricing appendix that captures: Net 30 w/2% early-pay, Net 60 baseline pricing delta, and release processing fee waiver for first two ramp releases. (Vanessa — target EOD Wed)
2) Rachel to provide a sample invoice mapping our internal SKU fields to Helix's GL/BU columns and to generate one sample invoice (PDF) for Helix finance to validate. (Rachel — target Tue EOD)
3) Ben to open a short order-form amendment in DocuSign that defines: PO vs release-id semantics, invoice metadata requirements, and acceptance criteria for invoice matching. I will include a 1-paragraph fallback: if invoice matching fails more than twice in the first 60 days, Redwood will suspend phased invoicing and revert to monthly consolidated invoices until mappings are resolved.

Ben opened the DocuSign envelope here: https://www.docusign.com/sign/ABCDEF123456 — legal will route to Helix once Vanessa's appendix and Rachel's sample invoice are attached.
